title: Experiment 6 – CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check)
description: Implementation of Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) error detection using modulo-2 polynomial division.
aim: To write a C program to implement Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) error detection technique.
theory: CRC is an error-detecting code based on polynomial arithmetic modulo 2. The sender generates a codeword by appending remainder bits from dividing data bits by a predetermined generator polynomial. The receiver performs the same division; a non-zero remainder indicates transmission error.
algorithm: Read data bits and generator polynomial bits.
Append (m - 1) zeros to the data bits, where m is the generator length.
Perform modulo-2 binary division using XOR operations.
Append the resulting (m - 1) remainder bits to original data to construct the transmitted codeword.
At receiver, perform modulo-2 division on received codeword with generator polynomial.
If remainder is all zeros report no error; otherwise report error detected.
